skill.name: sprint-planner
skill.description: Facilitates agile sprint planning by structuring goals, capacity, story estimates, backlog commitments, risks, and definition of done.
skill.summary: Plan agile sprints with capacity-aware backlog selection, goals, risks, and done criteria.
skill.author: shubhamsaboo

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive caused by a markdown code fence in SKILL.md lines 35-57. I found no executable code, command instructions, network use, environment access, prompt injection, or data exfiltration intent in the reviewed file.

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md line 35 begins a fenced markdown output template that ends at line 57. It contains sprint planning headings and checklists, not Ruby backtick execution or a command execution instruction.

content.user_title: Plan Agile Sprints With Clear Capacity
content.value_statement: Sprint planning often stalls when scope, estimates, and capacity are unclear. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to create sprint goals, backlog tables, risks, and done criteria.
actual_capabilities: Identifies sprint planning needs for agile, scrum, story points, capacity, and backlog prioritization.
Uses Modified Fibonacci estimates with 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, and 20 point options.
Applies team size, sprint days, hours, and a 0.6 to 0.8 focus factor to capacity planning.
Uses average velocity from the last 3 to 5 sprints as planning context.
Produces sprint goals, backlog tables, risks, mitigations, and definition of done checklists.
limitations: Does not integrate directly with issue trackers, calendars, or agile reporting systems.
Requires accurate backlog, team availability, and recent velocity from the user.
Does not replace team discussion, product owner decisions, or scrum master judgment.
Does not validate estimates against historical delivery data automatically.

use_cases.title: Prepare Sprint Planning
use_cases.description: Create a structured plan with capacity, candidate backlog items, dependencies, and a clear sprint goal.

use_cases.title: Align Scope With Goals
use_cases.description: Turn product priorities into a sprint-ready backlog that supports a specific business outcome.

use_cases.title: Balance Team Load
use_cases.description: Compare estimated work with team capacity before the team commits to sprint scope.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Sprint Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning with a small backlog
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a two-week sprint for this backlog. Include a sprint goal, capacity, committed points, sprint backlog table, risks, and definition of done.

prompt_templates.title: Estimate and Select Stories
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these user stories, suggest Modified Fibonacci point estimates, and select a realistic sprint backlog based on our team capacity.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Capacity Constraints
prompt_templates.prompt: Our team has reduced availability this sprint. Calculate practical capacity, flag overcommitment risks, and recommend which backlog items to defer.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Risk-Aware Sprint Commitment
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a sprint plan for these prioritized stories. Account for dependencies, recent velocity, delivery risks, mitigation actions, and acceptance readiness.

output_examples.input: Plan Sprint 12 for a team with 48 available focus hours and five prioritized stories.
output_examples.output: Sprint 12 includes a measurable goal, 21 committed points, a backlog table with owners, two dependency risks, and a definition of done checklist.

output_examples.input: Review this backlog and reduce scope for a team member on vacation.
output_examples.output: The plan lowers capacity, removes the least critical 8-point story, keeps the sprint goal intact, and lists the deferred work.

output_examples.input: Create a sprint plan for a release hardening sprint.
output_examples.output: The output prioritizes bug fixes, validation work, staging readiness, risk mitigation, and product owner approval before release.

best_practices: Provide team size, sprint dates, focus factor, recent velocity, and known time off.
Include story IDs, acceptance criteria, dependencies, and priority when requesting a sprint plan.
Use the generated plan as a facilitation aid and confirm commitments with the team.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill to force commitments without team agreement.
Do not treat point estimates as exact delivery guarantees.
Do not omit dependencies, blocked work, or planned absences from the planning input.

faq.question: What does this skill help plan?
faq.answer: It helps plan agile sprints with goals, capacity, story estimates, backlog scope, risks, and definition of done.

faq.question: Does it connect to Jira or other tools?
faq.answer: No. It works from information provided in the prompt and does not connect to external systems.

faq.question: Can it estimate story points?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses a Modified Fibonacci scale and can suggest estimates when story details are provided.

faq.question: What inputs improve the result?
faq.answer: Provide team availability, sprint length, recent velocity, backlog items, priorities, dependencies, and acceptance criteria.

faq.question: Can it choose the final sprint commitment?
faq.answer: It can recommend a commitment, but the team and product owner should confirm the final scope.

faq.question: Is it suitable for non-scrum teams?
faq.answer: It is best for scrum-style sprint planning, but kanban or hybrid teams can adapt the structure.
